root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: WeepingStones makes bright, dry stone and secret wet shade into places where life gathers, and where tending a pool changes what lives in it. Its alien plants, grazers, fliers and caravan beasts give the oasis a life of its own. At the water, predators leave drinkers alone and a guilty attack brings the nearby wildlife against the attacker's faction; the dangerous work is in the fish pens. Moisture farmers catch breeders, stock and feed their pools, read their health, and choose what to harvest. Neglect and crowding can turn their stock into a vhorrin; rescuing the farm produces a feast, while other delicious catches carry a real cost in a colonist's peace of mind. Dewgourds, spice, dewsilk and huldu fur make the place worth working and trading with. The unique old gorrask carries a working condenser and a seasonal oasis: the colony can guide it, sell its next settling place, or kill it to take the machine onto a ship. Its two optional quests put money and captivity against protecting its freedom. These promises belong together, but the farm, the truce and the walking oasis each need their own demonstration.

asks.why: F3. The pool at the buyer's settlement is already promised; making it real is owed work, not a new feature to vote on. The unresolved part is who bears the risk between the sale and fulfilment.
asks.picture: A faction buys the crab's next season at its inhabited settlement, which respects the existing claim law. Before arrival, the crab dies or cannot get there. Today's Sell action pays immediately and records the buyer, but I found no delivery step that makes the buyer's season pool happen.

asks.text: What would the farmers need to see before they could honestly call that season “kept free”?
asks.decision: Define protection success where alive may still mean confined.
asks.author: Codex WeepingStones dry run 2026-11-10
asks.guess: Temporary shelter is fair, but success means it can leave under its own power and the farmers get the promised season at its water. I recommend proving an open route and an actual departure, rather than requiring it to survive every attack without help.
asks.tree_changes: A departure requirement needs an unobstructed route and observed movement after protection. Freedom to choose without a forced departure needs a defined confinement check. Temporary confinement needs a release deadline and a failure or delay state if the colony refuses. If survival alone expresses your intent, name that narrower success honestly while retaining the existing story's promised aftermath as coverage debt. No option offers to remove either quest.

asks.speaker: agent
asks.title: Alive, but no longer free
asks.why: F3. Your choice already opposes captivity to keeping it free. “Not dead when the timer ends” may be a cheaper, wrong version of that promise. A wall can also be temporary protection, so the exact boundary matters.
asks.picture: You accept the farmers' protection quest, wall the old crab inside the colony and defeat both hunter waves. The timer finishes with the crab alive behind those walls. The current quest's success route is its timer; it does not demonstrate the crab walking on or the farmers actually sharing its pool.

contradictions.text: Current vhakk prose promises ambush at pool drinkers, contrary to frozen §6 and accepted suppression. Correct the contradiction under existing law; do not ask whether to allow it.
Buyer and expiry fields/payout do not deliver the pool promised by item and letter; question a7 addresses risk allocation only, not whether fulfilment is owed.

Extraction drains water before Kill(null), providing neither guilty instigator nor normal damaging hit to truce. Original walking-array story explicitly said extraction at water is a first strike. No implementation of that consequence found.

Local old 14/min7/55-degree heat data and fixed low-sun arrival advice predate later one-Direct-Sun ruling. Direct neighbours still read extension values; final composed patch/load not verified. Existing ruling governs, not a new per-biome tuning question.

Unconditional autonomous harvest plus nearest-pen stocking can erase breeder reserves; no demonstrated self-sustaining stock curve. Vanilla reproduction data is present, so absence of a custom breeding kernel is not proof nothing can reproduce.

Ivvol protection, crowded-only fan-eel escape, species-specific catch methods and body-temperature/keeper cues exceed present generic mechanics. Later huldu art prose calls it a hunter while thought still says it clung to the handler. Existing corpus needs reconciliation, not invented owner approval.

Walk/About include obsolete counts, donors, one-setting claim, ambrosia keep and placeholder-art language. Current XML/code wins implementation inventory; path history does not certify the current experience.

failure_modes: F1 — The oasis never becomes a readable, sustainable farm: automatic work empties stock, hunger/crowding turns wrong without a useful warning, and a cull message substitutes for recovery. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md; src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Source/RM_WorkGiver_HarvestPoolPen.cs:64; src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Source/RM_PoolBody.cs:82.

F2 — It is ordinary desert production with alien labels: wet shade and gathered life do not read, predator fiction contradicts the safe water, and good food has no felt unease. Sources: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/weeping_stones.md; src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_WeepingStonesNatives.xml:691; src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Defs/ThoughtDefs/RM_StockedPoolThoughts.xml.

F3 — The walking oasis' choices say more than they do: guidance floods unintended land, sale pays for undelivered water, extraction evades the truce, or a caged survivor counts as kept free. Sources: src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Source/RM_WalkingCondenser.cs; src/RimMandrake/WeepingStones/Defs/QuestScriptDefs/RM_CondenserQuests.xml; OWNER:1790972004219944071.
